strengths: The all-input converse covers arbitrary finite-energy inputs by separating low-information inputs from inputs close to the signal capacity. It does not infer a capacity converse from thermal-input evaluation or assume a thermal optimizer for the reset mixture.

The bounded Choi order, fixed-reference pinching, normalized comparator and established TRE inequality control branch discrimination throughout each prescribed n(E)=o(E) path. The explicit R_minus and the infinite-reference compression step were checked in review620.

Input/output truncation and exact type-space blocking preserve the physical expected input cost and yield one EA encoder/decoder for the arbitrary-index reset family without imposing reset energy. The coding limit is taken first at each fixed family.

Uniform matching covers all finite Shannon and fixed finite super-Shannon budgets, including endpoints and changing budgets. The unknown fixed signal extension uses a known sublinear envelope and orders only the signal channel; its worst-pair converse and linear-noise boundary example were checked.
weaknesses: R1 remains unresolved in this exact PDF: page 6, main.tex lines 456–458 cite Berta–Gharibyan–Walter Lemma 9 for the exact-type information bound. That lemma supplies compound achievability. Cite the earlier entropy/optical paper's Lemma 3 or include the short relative-entropy proof; retain Berta et al. for coding. The inequality itself was checked and is valid, so this is nonmaterial.

S1 remains an optional, nonblocking suggestion: on page 5, Eq.(14), display the short thermal-tail mutual-information derivation of U_E supplied in report section 6. Its loose coefficients were found valid; this is an exposition improvement, not a necessary repair of the theorem.

The earlier entropy/optical paper already supplies the entropy-budget curve, witness family, spectral matching, type blocking and pure-loss common-code extension. Gaussian extremality, Choi order, mixture inequalities, TRE, continuity and compound coding are established ingredients; they are not new results here.

Literature searching was directed, not exhaustive. Selected primary statements and proof passages were read, with versions and hashes retained. Full BSST, one-shot decoupling, AEP and every imported lemma were not re-proved. Shirokov's selected passage states and cites the mixture bound; its original cited proof was not newly fetched, though the needed finite-entropy case was checked directly. Catalano's selected model passages were read, not its complete appendix proofs or numerical suite.

The 90 scalar checks used 180 decimal digits; the 72 seeded noncommuting finite-matrix checks had maximum reported identity discrepancy 3.1086244689504383e-15. Byte-identical replay corroborates finite identities only. It is not independent code, an operational common code, Gaussian capacity optimization, a test of the infinite Choi form or an asymptotic proof.

The result fixes lambda, kappa and alpha=1 or finite alpha>1. It does not give uniformity at singular parameter boundaries, for alpha varying with energy, or across all unspecified sublinear paths at a fixed energy. All channel parameters are fixed within each code; the unknown-signal case requires a known envelope.

No efficient code, uniform finite-blocklength estimate, exact finite-energy mixed-channel capacity, complete critical/superlinear-noise classification or general necessity of n=o(E) is established. The linear-noise example excludes one proposed extension; it does not solve the critical regime. This model report is not human peer review, formal verification, a priority certificate or editorial acceptance.
